login.note: Sign-in is delegated to Instagram: the page offers 'Continue with Instagram' (an instagram.com handshake that lands back on threads.com) or a direct username/password form for a Threads-only account. A human must complete it, and the Instagram hop means the browser leaves this origin and comes back — do not close the window mid-handshake.

logout.note: No logout URL that can be visited. Log out through the '...' / settings menu in the web UI. Because sign-in came from Instagram, logging out of Threads does not log the profile out of instagram.com and vice versa — check both if the intent is a clean profile.

traps: threads.net IS NOT THE ORIGIN ANY MORE. Meta moved the app to threads.com in April 2025 and reversed the redirect: https://threads.net/ answers 301 -> https://www.threads.com/ (verified 2026-09-12). Cookies, localStorage and any probe are origin-scoped, so a probe pinned to threads.net is either measuring an empty origin or measuring whatever it landed on after a cross-origin redirect. This file keeps the .net name because that is what people still type; every URL in it points at threads.com.

The CurrentUserInitialData blob is present on the SIGNED-OUT page, with ACCOUNT_ID and USER_ID as the string "0" and NAME as the empty string (verified on a signed-out www.threads.com document, 2026-09-12). Presence is not the verdict; USER_ID != "0" is. Note they are strings, not numbers.

The session cookie (sessionid) is HttpOnly and invisible to document.cookie. ds_user_id is the readable half of the same session — the same split as instagram.com — so it can corroborate a verdict but can never carry one on its own, and it can outlive the session it names.

The feed is GraphQL-hydrated after load (POST /api/graphql with a doc_id, fb_dtsg and an LSD token minted in the page). The HTML that arrives carries chrome and config, not posts, so a DOM read taken too early returns an empty feed that is indistinguishable from an account with nothing to show.

Meta serves a logged-out-looking shell to clients it does not trust, and answers rate limiting with a normal-looking 200 page and no content rather than a 429. An empty result here means 'ask again later, with the real profile', not 'there is nothing'.
notes: PROBE STRATEGY: (a) the site's own embedded state object. Meta web pages ship a CurrentUserInitialData record inside their data-sjs script payloads, and on Threads it answers the question literally: {"ACCOUNT_ID":"0","USER_ID":"0","NAME":""} when signed out (verified against a real signed-out document on 2026-09-12), and a numeric id plus a display NAME when signed in. The probe scans the inline scripts for that record, gates on USER_ID != "0", and reports NAME. The readable ds_user_id cookie is used only as corroboration in `why`, and the one case where they disagree (USER_ID "0" but ds_user_id present, i.e. a cached or logged-out shell served to a live session) is reported as signed_in with an explicit warning to re-probe rather than as a silent verdict either way. document.cookie is wrapped because it throws SecurityError on an opaque origin. WHAT A READ RECIPE SHOULD DO: the DOM is a last resort; the real path is the same GraphQL endpoint the page uses. Capture a real feed/profile request first (recipe-builder), then replay POST https://www.threads.com/api/graphql with the page's fb_dtsg, LSD token, X-IG-App-ID and the doc_id for the query, reading posts out of the JSON. doc_ids rotate without warning, so a recipe must fail loudly on a missing doc_id instead of returning an empty list. A cheap read-only fallback for a single profile is the server-rendered https://www.threads.com/@<handle> document, whose data-sjs blobs contain the posts before any hydration. WRITE: empty. Posting goes through the same GraphQL surface and is not documented anywhere stable enough to write down as a verb.
